messages:
maria: follow-up from today's all-hands on pricing/quotas  three quick customer scenarios that came up: API-key sharing across microservices, per-route quotas, and emergency card-topup UX. can we clarify behavior and docs?
phil: good pack. which should we tackle first?
dena: API-key sharing case: customer has one key used by multiple small services. if one service spikes and burns credits, we need clear rules for attribution and notifications. they were confused why another service got 429s.
ryan: attribution today is by API key. if you share a key, you're sharing the bucket. we recommend per-service keys to isolate quotas. console shows per-key usage but not per-client metadata unless you pass `client_id` in headers.
maria: can we recommend best-practices in docs e.g., create per-service API keys, use org-pooled credits if you want shared billing, and set `quota_behavior` to `graceful` for UX sensitive services?
dena: yes please. also add a snippet to rotate keys and map old->new in the console to avoid losing continuity.
phil: second: per-route quotas. customers asked for route-level throttles so a heavy embedding route doesn't starve chat. current system has per-key and per-organization buckets plus model-level soft quotas.
ryan: design idea: allow route-level sub-buckets that consume from the parent API key bucket but have local limits. semantics: once route-sub-bucket hits local cap, you get `route_quota_exceeded` not the global `quota_exceeded`. console should show both.
consequence: local caps must be enforced atomically to avoid overcommit when many routes race. implementation is a token reservation step on request.
phil: third: emergency card-topup UX. customers want a one-click "emergency topup" for org admins with a clear cost preview and immediate unblocking? what's current policy?
billing-bot: current: auto-topup via card-on-file happens automatically for account overages. manual emergency one-off charges require support intervention.
maria: product ask: can we make a one-click "emergency topup" for org admins with a clear cost preview and immediate unblocking?
dena: feasibility questions: PCI concerns? we already tokenize cards but charging immediately and extending quotas needs ledger hooks and immediate quota refresh across edge caches.
legal-bot: add legal note: emergency topup UI must include clear language on refunds, charge disputes, and require a primary org admin to confirm. store consent audit.
ryan: infra notes: to avoid race, topup should create a ledger credit then publish a cache-invalidation event. edges should accept the new balance within ~5s. try to keep window <10s for best UX.
phil: edge case: what if topup succeeds but request already failed with 429 and client retried and got duplicate processing? we need idempotency guidance. propose include a `request_id` header and advise clients to dedupe replays.
maria: another subtlety: mid-stream topup for SSE/WS. if payment clears mid-stream do we resume or instruct client to reconnect? customers prefer transparent resume if possible.
dena: practical approach: if SSE/WS session maintains connection, we can continue streaming after emitting `billing_status: cleared` event. if connection was closed we require reconnect which will see the new balance. SDKs should handle `billing_status` event.
phil: billing question: do we bill grace overage from emergency topup differently? e.g., overage consumed before topup vs after. need clear accounting.
billing-bot: policy: ledger records the time window. charges are applied in chronological order; overage consumed before topup remains billed and topup replenishes new bucket forward. we will add a `ledger_event_id` to the billing response to aid reconciliation.
legal-bot: flag: emergency topup should not be marketed as a replacement for proper budget controls. include default limits and require org admin acknowledgement to prevent abuse.
phil: docs action items: 1) best-practices guide for API key per-service + header metadata (owner @dena). 2) spec for route-level sub-buckets and error codes (owner @ryan). 3) product + billing design for emergency topup UX with cost preview, audit trail, and edge-invalidation (owner @phil + billing). 4) SDK surface for `billing_status` and `request_id` dedupe (owner @dena).
maria: thanks. can owners drop short proposals in the all-hands PR by Wednesday EOD? we'll review at next sync. :thumbsup:
